Chapter 2: Skeptical or Guarded.
Ever notice how some people seem to keep their guard up, almost as if they're holding back until they're sure it's safe? That's what we're diving into right now.
When someone's skeptical or guarded, they're not being unfriendly—they're just testing the waters. Maybe they've been burned before. Maybe they're just careful about who they trust. Sound familiar?
Imagine you're meeting someone new. You throw out a friendly question, but they give you a short answer, maybe even avoid eye contact. It's not that they don't want to connect. They're just trying to figure out, "Can I really open up here?"
So, what do you do? Well, patience is your best friend. Offer genuine warmth, but don't push too hard. Sometimes, the smallest gestures—like remembering their name or following up on something they mentioned—can show you're safe.
Think about situations where you’ve felt skeptical or guarded yourself. Maybe at a new job, or meeting your partner's friends for the first time. It takes a little time to lower those walls, right?
Here’s something to pay attention to: When you sense someone is hesitant, focus on creating a space where they don’t feel judged. Ask open-ended questions, listen more than you speak, and let trust build naturally.
The key takeaway? If you’re patient and consistent, you’ll often find those initial walls start to come down. And that’s when real, meaningful connections can happen.
